JISHUMI:v2p1561/r13.claim: The waw in asaw is plural; the damma meets two consonants when the usual kasra is blocked.
JISHUMI:v2p1561/r13.anchor: لأنه واو الجمع، فأما حركتها فلالتقاء الساكنين، وأصل الحركة في التقاء الساكنين الكسرة،

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r1.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r1.claim: Hasan reconciles the denial elsewhere through different afterlife stations: whispering, denial, confession, and asking to return.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r1.anchor: الأول: أن في الآخرة مواطن ومقامات، ففي موطن لا تسمع إلا همسا، وفي موطن يكذبون، ويقولون: والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين، وفي موضع يعترفون ويسألون الرجعة عن الحسن.

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says not concealing is part of their wish, after their limbs expose them.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r2.anchor: الثاني: (ولا يكتمون) داخل في التمني بعد ما نطقت جوارحهم لفضيحتهم عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r3.claim: Another explanation is concealment does not count because it is manifest to God.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r3.anchor: الثالث: لا يعتد بكتمانهم؛ لأنه ظاهر عند الله تعالى.

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r4.claim: A fourth explanation says they report their own understanding without intending concealment until truth becomes clear.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r4.anchor: الرابع: أنهم لم يقصدوا الكتمان وإنما أخبروا على حسب ما توهموا تقديره: والله ما كنا مشركين عند أنفسنا

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r5.claim: Abu Ali says “See how they lied” refers to worldly lying; the author agrees because nobody lies in the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r5.anchor: وقوله: (انظر كيف كذبوا) يعني في الدنيا عن أبي علي وهو الصحيح؛ لأن الآخرة لا يجوز أن يكذب فيه أحد

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r6.claim: Prophets testify against communities about their deeds.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r6.anchor: تدل الآية على أن الأنبياء يشهدون على أممهم بأعمالهم

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r7.claim: Witness testimony heightens the negligent's remorse and believers' joy, explaining why deniers wish the earth would level over them.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r7.anchor: أحدها: زيادة حسرة للمقصرين وسرور المؤمنين، ولذلك تمنى الكافر عند هذه الشهادة

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r8.claim: Public testimony shows God recompenses each person justly, exposing the Mujabbira's false accusations.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r8.anchor: لما يظهر عند الخلائق أنه تعالى يجازي كل أحد بعمله وأنه لا يظلم أحدا

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r9.claim: Picturing the scene is a great kindness encouraging obedience and avoidance of sin.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r9.anchor: أن تصور هذه الحالة لطفا عظيما للمكلفين في الإقدام على الطاعات والانتهاء عن المعاصي

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r10.claim: A report says the Prophet asked Ibn Masud to recite; when he reached the verse, Ibn Masud wept and stopped.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r10.anchor: وقد روي أن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم - أمر ابن مسعود أن يقرأ عليه القرآن، فقرأ سورة النساء، فلما بلغ هذه الآية

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r11.claim: The author offers possible reasons for Ibn Masud's tears: gratitude for the Prophet's station or compassion for sinners.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r11.anchor: ويحتمل أن بكاءه كان شكرا لله تعالى على هذا المحل الشريف، ويحتمل أنه كان إشفاقا على المقصرين

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r12.claim: Every community has a witness, who may be a prophet or another person; the text alone does not determine which, though either is rationally possible.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r12.anchor: وتدل على أن في كل أمة شهيدا يشهد عليهم، ثم ذلك الشهيد يكون نبيا أو غير نبي يقف على دليل سمعي

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r13.claim: The verse does not prove that every era must have an infallible person, because witnessing does not require infallibility.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r13.anchor: وكلا الوجهين يجوز عقلا ولا حجة فيه للإمامية أنه لا بد في كل زمان من معصوم؛ لأنه ليس من شرط الشهادة العصمة

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r14.claim: The witness could mean angels or believers; “you” is taken as the Prophet because the address points to him.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r14.anchor: ولو تأوله متأول على الملائكة أو على المؤمنين لم يبعد، وإنما حملنا بك على النبي

JISHUMI:v2p1563/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r15.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r15.claim: Abu Ali requires people upholding truth in every era, though the author says this is not a condition.
JISHUMI:v2p1563/r15.anchor: على أن عند أبي علي لا بد في كل عصر من قوم يقومون بالحق، وإن كان ذلك عندنا ليس بشرط.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r9.claim: One interpretation is that the unbelievers wish to be made level with the earth, as in 78:40 where the unbeliever wishes he were dust.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r9.anchor: فيه قولان : أحدهما : أن الذين تمنوه من تسوية الأرض بهم , أن يجعلهم مثلها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r10.claim: The other interpretation is that they wish the earth would open so that they could disappear into its depths.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p488/r10.anchor: والثاني : أنهم تمنوا لو انفتحت لهم الأرض فصاروا في بطنها

MUQATIL:4:40-42/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:40-42/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:40-42/r6.claim: After denying that they were polytheists, the disbelievers' body parts testify to the shirk their tongues concealed; they wish the earth would split open and level over them.
MUQATIL:4:40-42/r6.anchor: وذلك بأنهم قالوا فى الآخرة: والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين، فشهدت عليهم الجوارح بما كتمت ألسنتهم من الشرك،

MUQATIL:4:40-42/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:40-42/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:40-42/r7.claim: They cannot hide anything from God because their limbs testify against them.
MUQATIL:4:40-42/r7.anchor: { ولا يكتمون الله حديثا } [آية: 42]، يعنى الجوارح حين شهدت عليهم.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r1.claim: The time phrase يومئذ modifies the wish of those who disbelieved.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r1.anchor: يومئذ ﴾ ظرف لقوله ﴿ يود الذين كفروا ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r2.claim: They wish they were buried and leveled with the earth as the dead are.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r2.anchor: لو يدفنون فتسوى بهم الأرض كما تسوى بالموتى أو يودون

NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that they wish they had never been raised and were still equal with the earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r3.anchor: أو يودون أنهم لم يبعثوا و أنهم كانوا و الأرض سواء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r4.claim: They may also wish to become like beasts that turn to dust.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r4.anchor: أو تصير البهائم ترابا فيودون حالها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r5.speaker: حمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read taswā with fatḥa, a light sīn, imāla, and deletion of one tāʾ from the doubled form.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r5.anchor: بفتح التاء وتخفيف السين والامالة وحذف إحدى التاءين من تتسوى حمزة وعلى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r6.speaker: مدنى وشامى
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r6.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers assimilate the tāʾ into the sīn in taswā.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r6.anchor: تسوى بادغام التاء فى السين مدنى وشامى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r7.claim: They cannot hide anything from God because their bodily members testify against them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p223#2/r7.anchor: مستأنف أى ولا يقدرون على كتمانه لأن جوارحهم تشهد عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r1.claim: The waw in عصوا takes damma to resolve the meeting of two quiescent letters; kasra is also permissible.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r2.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read تسوى with an open ta and doubled sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «تسوى» بفتح التاء والتشديد في السين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read with an open ta and a light sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r3.anchor: وحمزة والكسائي كذلك إلا أنهما خففا السين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r4.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r4.claim: The other readers use a damma on the ta and a light sin, making the verb passive with its agent unspecified.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r4.anchor: والباقون ضموا التاء وخففوا السين، مبنيا للمفعول والفاعل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r5.claim: One interpretation has God make the disbelievers level with the earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r5.anchor: والمعنى لو يسوي الله بهم الأرض، أي يجعلهم والأرض سواء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that they wish they had never been resurrected and that the earth had remained level over them, since they were made from dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r6.anchor: ومعنى آخر: تمنوا لو لم يبعثهم الله وكانت الأرض مستوية عليهم لأنهم من التراب نقلوا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r7.claim: On the first two readings the earth is the subject: they wish it would open and swallow them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r7.anchor: وعلى القراءة الأولى والثانية فالأرض فاعلة، والمعنى تمنوا لو انفتحت لهم الأرض فساخوا فيها قاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r8.claim: Al-Hasan takes the preposition ب as meaning على: they wish the earth would split and flatten over them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r8.anchor: وقيل: الباء بمعنى على، أي لو تسوى عليهم أي تنشق فتسوى عليهم عن الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r9.claim: The doubled reading reflects assimilation; the light reading reflects omission of the second ta.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r9.anchor: فقراءة التشديد على الإدغام، والتخفيف على حذف التاء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r10.claim: Some say they wish this after seeing animals turned to dust and realizing they themselves are to remain eternally in Hell, as in the verse saying the disbeliever wishes to be dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r10.anchor: وقيل: إنما تمنوا هذا حين رأوا البهائم تصير ترابا وعلموا أنهم مخلدون في النار

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r11.claim: Another account places the wish when earlier nations challenge this community's testimony; after the Prophet attests to their integrity, the polytheists deny their shirk, their mouths are sealed, and limbs testify, so they wish to be swallowed by earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r11.anchor: وقيل: إنما تمنوا هذا حين شهدت هذه الأمة للأنبياء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r12.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports one analysis in which the clause begins a new sentence: their deeds are manifest to God and cannot be hidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r12.anchor: قال الزجاج قال بعضهم: { ولا يكتمون الله حديثا }. مستأنف لأن ما عملوه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r13.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj also reports a coordinated reading: they wish the earth were leveled over them and wish they had not concealed anything from God, since their lies have been exposed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r13.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو معطوف، والمعنى يود لو أن الأرض سويت بهم وأنهم لم يكتموا الله حديثا لأنه ظهر كذبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that when people see only Muslims enter Paradise, the polytheists deny shirk; God seals their mouths and their hands and feet speak, so they can no longer conceal anything.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r14.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس عن هذه الآية، وعن قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r15.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r15.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the afterlife has different stages: concealment occurs at some stages, while after matters become clear and reckoning begins they do not conceal.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:42/r15.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: الآخرة مواطن يكون هذا في بعضها وهذا في بعضها

QASHANI:4:42-43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r1.claim: Disbelievers are veiled from truth, and disobeying the Messenger is veiling from religion.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r1.anchor: بالاحتجاب عن الحق { وعصوا الرسول } بالاحتجاب عن الدين

QASHANI:4:42-43/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r2.claim: They wish the earth of preparedness leveled so their souls are erased or left blank of false beliefs and ruinous vices.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r2.anchor: أرض الاستعداد، فتنطمس نفوسهم أو تصير ساذجة لا نقش فيها

QASHANI:4:42-43/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:42-43/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:42-43/r3.claim: They cannot conceal any imprint in their souls to escape punishment for it.
QASHANI:4:42-43/r3.anchor: أي: لا يقدرون على كتم حديث من تلك النقوش حتى لا يتعذبون بعقابه.

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r1.claim: Conjoining ‘disobeyed the Messenger’ to ‘disbelieved’ means the disobedience differs from disbelief, since a thing cannot be conjoined to itself.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r1.anchor: لأن عطف الشيء على نفسه غير جائز ، فوجب حمل عصيان الرسول على المعاصي المغايرة للكفر

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r2.claim: The verse therefore indicates that unbelievers are addressed by Islam’s practical obligations and punished for those sins in addition to disbelief; otherwise mentioning their disobedience here would serve no purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r2.anchor: إذا ثبت هذا فنقول : الآية دالة على أن الكفار مخاطبون بفروع الاسلام

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, and Abū ʿAmr read tusawwā with passive construction: tāʾ vowelled ḍamma and light sīn.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو { تسوى } مضمومة التاء خفيفة السين

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r4.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read with fatḥa on tāʾ and doubled sīn, meaning ‘become level’; the tāʾ assimilates into the nearby sīn, a pattern also found at 27:47, 10:24, and 6:26.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر { تسوى } مفتوحة التاء مشددة السين بمعنى : تتسوى

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r5.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with fatḥa on tāʾ and light sīn, dropping the tāʾ that Nāfiʿ assimilates.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { لو تسوى } مفتوحة التاء والسين خفيفة

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r6.speaker: مفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r6.claim: One interpretation is that they wish to be buried and covered by earth as the dead are.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r6.anchor: الأول : لو يدفنون فتسوى بهم الأرض كما تسوى بالموتى

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r7.speaker: مفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r7.claim: A second interpretation is that they wish they had never been resurrected and had remained equal with the earth.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r7.anchor: والثاني : يودون أنهم لم يبعثوا وأنهم كانوا والأرض سواء

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r8.speaker: مفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r8.claim: A third interpretation is that animals will be turned to dust, and the disbelievers will wish to share their state, as in 78:40.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r8.anchor: الثالث : تصير البهائم ترابا فيودون حالها كقوله : { الكافر ياليتنى كنت ترابا }

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r9.claim: If the clause continues the preceding wish, Ibn ʿAbbās says they wish earth would close over them and that they had not concealed Muhammad’s message, disbelieved in him, or acted hypocritically.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r9.anchor: أحدهما : ما قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يودون لو تنطبق عليهم الأرض ولم يكونوا كتموا

RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r10.claim: Another connected reading has polytheists first deny their shirk when they see Muslims forgiven; God then seals their mouths and their limbs testify to their deeds, so they wish they had been earth and had not denied the truth.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86/r10.anchor: الثاني : أن المشركين لما رأوا يوم القيامة أن الله تعالى يغفر لأهل الاسلام ولا يغفر

RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r1.claim: A second exegetical approach treats this as a new sentence: their deeds are manifest to God, so they cannot possibly conceal them.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r1.anchor: الطريق الثاني في التأويل : أن هذا الكلام مستأنف ، فإن ما عملوه ظاهر عند الله ، فكيف

RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r2.claim: The statements that they will not conceal the truth and that they will deny being polytheists at 6:23 concern different stages of Judgment: some are silent, some speak and lie, some confess and ask to return, and finally their mouths are sealed while their limbs testify.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r2.anchor: أن مواطن القيامة كثيرة ، فموطن لا يتكلمون فيه وهو قوله : { فلا تسمع إلا همسا }

RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r3.claim: A second reconciliation says the denial never actually occurs; it is only part of what they wish they had not done.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : أن هذا الكتمان غير واقع ، بل هو داخل في التمني على ما بينا

RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r4.claim: A third says they did not intend concealment: they spoke according to what they had thought, considering themselves right until the truth became clear.
RAZI-FULL:v10p86#2/r4.anchor: الثالث : أنهم لم يقصدوا الكتمان ، وإنما أخبروا على حسب ما توهموا

STUDYQURAN:4:42/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r1.claim: That Day is the day the prophetic witnesses are called forth, as described in 4:41.
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r1.anchor: On that Day—that is, the day the prophetic witnesses will be called forth (v. 41)—

STUDYQURAN:4:42/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r2.claim: Terrified of accountability, disbelievers will wish to be level with earth, invisible and unaccountable, even nonexistent; dust would be preferable to punishment in the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r2.anchor: they will long to be level with the earth, that is, to be unnoticeable and so not accountable

STUDYQURAN:4:42/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r3.claim: The wish to be level with the earth may also mean wanting the earth to swallow them or cave in beneath them.
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r3.anchor: The disbelievers’ wish to be level with the earth may also connote a desire that the earth devour them or cave in below them

STUDYQURAN:4:42/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r4.claim: The earth is the active subject in the Arabic construction, supporting the interpretation that it swallows or caves in beneath them.
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r4.anchor: for the earth is the active subject in the Arabic construction here

STUDYQURAN:4:42/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r5.claim: Their wish echoes the disbelievers’ lament in 78:40, Oh, would that I were dust.
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r5.anchor: This is similar to the lament of the disbelievers in 78:40

STUDYQURAN:4:42/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r6.claim: Nothing can be hidden from God: even if people lie about their deeds, their body parts will testify on Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:4:42/r6.anchor: even if people seek to lie about what they did in life, their own body parts will testify against them on the Day of Judgment

TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains that the disbelievers wish to be made dust by God's creative act.
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r1.anchor: لأن من تمنى منهم أن يكون يومئذ ترابا إنما يتمنى أن يكون كذلك بتكوين الله إياه كذلك

TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r2.claim: Meccan, Medinan, and Hijazi readers use a doubled form; Kufans read with a light sīn; another reading makes God level them with earth. All mean they become dust, and all are valid.
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r2.anchor: قرأته عامة قراء أهل الحجاز ومكة والمدينة: (لو تسوى بهم الأرض) بتشديد السين والواو وفتح التاء

TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the light-sīn reading, avoiding two doubled consonants and matching 78:40, where the disbeliever wishes he were dust rather than explicitly saying he wishes the earth leveled over him.
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r3.anchor: فأعجب القراءة إلي في ذلك: لو تسوى بهم الأرض، بفتح التاء وتخفيف السين، كراهية الجمع بين تشديدين في حرف واحد

TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r4.claim: Their bodily organs will disclose what their mouths might deny, so they cannot conceal anything from God.
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r4.anchor: ولا تكتم الله جوارحهم حديثا وإن جحدت ذلك أفواههم

TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that after the polytheists decide to deny their shirk, God seals their mouths and their hands and feet speak, resolving their denial in 6:23.
TAB-FULL:v7p40#2/r5.anchor: فختم الله على أفواههم، وتكلمت أيديهم وأرجلهم، فلا يكتمون الله حديثا

TAB-FULL:v7p43/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r1.claim: The day is when God brings a witness from every community and Muhammad as witness over his community; the unbelievers are those who deny God's oneness and disobey His Messenger.
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أما قوله: {ثم لم تكن فتنتهم

TAB-FULL:v7p43/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reconciles 6:23 with this verse: unbelievers first deny shirk hoping for forgiveness, but their mouths are sealed and their limbs testify, after which they wish to be leveled with earth and can no longer conceal anything.
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أما قوله: {ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين}

TAB-FULL:v7p43/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r3.claim: In Ibn Abbas's reply to Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq, people gather in one place; the polytheists deny shirk, but their limbs testify against them, so they wish the earth were leveled over them and stop concealing the truth.
TAB-FULL:v7p43/r3.anchor: فقال له ابن عباس: إني أحسبك قمت من عند أصحابك فقلت: ألقى علي ابن عباس متشابه القرآن

TAB-FULL:v7p45/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v7p45/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the wish as having the earth, with its mountains, leveled over them; on this reading they wish they had been made level with the earth and had not concealed anything from God.
TAB-FULL:v7p45/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {يومئذ يود الذين كفروا وعصوا الرسول لو تسوى بهم الأرض

TAB-FULL:v7p45/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p45/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p45/r2.claim: Other interpreters take the clauses as saying that they will not conceal anything from God and will wish the earth leveled over them; their speech cannot hide anything from God's all-encompassing knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v7p45/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك يومئذ لا يكتمون الله حديثا، ويودون لو تسوى بهم الأرض.

TABATABAI:4:36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:36/r1.claim: These seven verses urge kindness and spending for God, promise a beautiful reward, and condemn withholding or spending for show.
TABATABAI:4:36/r1.anchor: آيات سبع فيها حث على الإحسان والإنفاق في سبيل الله ووعد جميل عليه وذم على تركه

TABATABAI:4:40-42/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r8.claim: Calling them disobedient to the Messenger refers to defying commands issued from his authority as guardian, not disobeying God's legal rulings.
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r8.anchor: نسبة المعصية إلى الرسول يشهد أن المراد بها معصية أوامره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الصادرة عن مقام ولايته

TABATABAI:4:40-42/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r9.claim: Their wish that the earth be leveled over them is a metaphor for death and cancellation of existence, like the wish in al-Nabaʾ 78:40.
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r9.anchor: كناية عن الموت بمعنى بطلان الوجود نظير قوله تعالى ويقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا

TABATABAI:4:40-42/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r10.claim: The clause is coordinated with the syntactic position of yūddu; it explains their wish for death because they cannot conceal anything from God.
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r10.anchor: وفائدته الدلالة بوجه على ما يعلل به تمنيهم الموت

TABATABAI:4:40-42/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r11.claim: They stand exposed to God as their deeds are present and their limbs, prophets, angels, and others testify; their shameful acts are visible, so they cannot hide them.
TABATABAI:4:40-42/r11.anchor: لظهور حالهم عليه تعالى بحضور أعمالهم وشهادة أعضائهم وشهادة الأنبياء والملائكة وغيرهم عليهم

TABATABAI:4:36-42/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r6.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r6.claim: Musʿada ibn Ṣadaqa transmits from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad and his grandfather a sermon by Ali: at the Resurrection mouths are sealed, hands speak, feet testify, and skins disclose deeds. No grading is stated.
TABATABAI:4:36-42/r6.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في خطبة يصف هول يوم القيامة ختم على الأفواه فلا تكلم وتكلمت الأيدي

AKHFASH:v1p258/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p258/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p258/r1.claim: Either their limbs cannot conceal anything from God, or the meaning is that nothing is hidden from Him even if they try to conceal it.
AKHFASH:v1p258/r1.anchor: أي: لا تكتمه الجوارح او يقول: "لا يخفى عليه وإن كتموه"

AKHFASH:v1p258/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p258/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p258/r2.claim: Both reported forms of تسوى are good readings.
AKHFASH:v1p258/r2.anchor: وقال {لو تسوى بهم الأرض} وقال بعضهم {تسوى} [و] كل حسن

TABRISI:4:41-42/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:41-42/r8.claim: Yawm idhin governs yود; idh is nunated to mark completion of the noun.
TABRISI:4:41-42/r8.anchor: والعامل في يومئذ يود بعد إذ ولم يجز ذلك في إذا جئنا

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r4.claim: The disbelievers wish they could be made level with earth, meaning they had never been raised and had remained as earth because they know the punishment and eternal Fire awaiting them.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r4.anchor:
معناه لو تجعلون والأرض سواء كما قال تعالى:
ويقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r5.claim: The phrase is connected to making fingertips into one flat surface, explaining تسوية as flattening and joining.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r5.anchor:
ومن التسوية قوله:
بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says they wish the gathered people would walk over them as they tread the earth.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن معناه يودون أن يمشي عليهم أهل الجمع

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r7.claim: Another report says animals will become dust on Judgment Day and disbelievers will wish they had become dust too.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r7.anchor: وروي أيضا أن البهائم يوم القيامة تصير ترابا

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r8.claim: The report about animals becoming dust is valid only if compensation ends; al-Tabrisi says this is correct, whereas those who hold compensation eternal reject it.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r8.anchor: وهذا لا يجيزه إلا من قال إن العوض منقطع وهو الصحيح

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas links the phrase to the wish: they wish they had not concealed anything after denying shirk and being exposed by their limbs.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r9.anchor: أي ويودون إن لو لم يكتموا الله حديثا

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r10.claim: A new-statement view says they ultimately confess worldly deeds and unbelief though they deny sins at some stages, thinking denial will help; Judgment has different stations.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r10.anchor: وثانيها: أنه كلام مستأنف والمراد به أنهم لا يكتمون الله شيئا

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r11.claim: Another view says they cannot hide anything because their limbs testify; the implied subject is their limbs, which do not conceal even if people do.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r11.anchor: فالتقدير لا تكتمه جوارحهم وإن كتموه

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r12.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r12.claim: Ata connects the wish to be leveled with earth to regret that they concealed Muhammad’s message and mission.

TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r13.speaker: أبو القاسم البلخي
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r13.claim: Al-Balkhi reads the verse literally: they cannot conceal because compelled to abandon wrongdoing and lies; their denial means they did not consider their own approach to God to be shirk.
TABRISI:4:41-42#2/r13.anchor: أن ذلك ليس بشرك من حيث تقربهم إلى الله عن أبي القاسم البلخي

FARRA:v1p268/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r5.claim: تسوى means that the unbelievers wish they could be made level with the soil.

FARRA:v1p268/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r6.claim: The beasts are turned to dust; after the unbelievers deny being idolaters, their mouths are sealed and their limbs testify, making them wish they were dust.

FARRA:v1p268/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r7.claim: In al-Farrāʾ’s first parse, “they would not conceal anything” belongs inside the unbelievers’ wish to have been made dust.
FARRA:v1p268/r7.anchor: فهنالك يودون أنهم كانوا ترابا ولم يكتموا الله حديثا. فكتمان الحديث

FARRA:v1p268/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p268/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p268/r8.claim: A second parse makes “they will not conceal anything from God” an independent statement followed by their wish that the earth be leveled over them.
FARRA:v1p268/r8.anchor: ويقال: إنما المعنى: يومئذ لا يكتمون الله حديثا ويودون لو تسوى

THALABI:v3p309/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p309/r15.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
THALABI:v3p309/r15.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers pronounce the ta open and stress sin, assimilating the second ta of the form into sin.
THALABI:v3p309/r15.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام بفتح التاء وتشديد السين، على معنى: تتسوى فأدغمت التاء بالسين

THALABI:v3p309/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p309/r16.speaker: أهل الكوفة إلا عاصما
THALABI:v3p309/r16.claim: Kufans except Asim read an open ta and light sin, omitting the second ta of the reflexive form, as in the quoted expression about no soul speaking without permission.
THALABI:v3p309/r16.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة إلا عاصما بفتح التاء وتخفيف السين، على حذف تاء تفعل، كقوله: لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه

THALABI:v3p309/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p309/r17.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v3p309/r17.claim: The remaining readers use a passive form with damma on ta and a light sin: the earth is leveled with them until they and it become one.
THALABI:v3p309/r17.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم التاء وتخفيف السين على المجهول، قالوا: سويت بهم الأرض وصاروا هم والأرض شيئا واحدا

THALABI:v3p309/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p309/r18.speaker: قتادة وعبيدة
THALABI:v3p309/r18.claim: Qatada and Ubayda say they wish the earth would move with them, return them to it as they emerged from it, and then cover them.
THALABI:v3p309/r18.anchor: وقال قتادة وعبيدة: يعني لو تحركت الأرض فساروا فيها، وعادوا إليها كما خرجوا منها، ثم تسوى عليهم حتى تعلوهم

THALABI:v3p309/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p309/r19.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v3p309/r19.claim: Ibn Kaysan says they wish they had never been resurrected, but had remained earth with the ground level over them.
THALABI:v3p309/r19.anchor: ابن كيسان: ودوا أنهم لم يبعثوا طرا، وإنما نقلوا من التراب وكانت الأرض مستوية بهم.

THALABI:v3p309/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p309/r20.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v3p309/r20.claim: Al-Kalbi says God will turn beasts and birds to dust, then level the earth with them, prompting unbelievers to wish they were dust walked over by the gathered people.
THALABI:v3p309/r20.anchor: الكلبي: يقول الله عز وجل للبهائم والوحش والطير والسباع: كن ترابا فتسوى بها الأرض

THALABI:v3p311/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسين
THALABI:v3p311/r1.claim: Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn reports an interpretation that they would ransom themselves with everything on earth; he adduces the criminal's wish to ransom himself with his sons.
THALABI:v3p311/r1.anchor: أستاذنا أبو القاسم الحسين أنه سمع من تأول هذه الآية

THALABI:v3p311/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311/r2.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v3p311/r2.claim: Ataa says they wish the earth were leveled over them and wish they had not concealed Muhammad's affair or description.
THALABI:v3p311/r2.anchor: قال عطاء: ودوا لو تسوى بهم الأرض، وإنهم لم يكونوا كتموا أمر محمد

THALABI:v3p311/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311/r3.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v3p311/r3.claim: Others take the clause as a new statement: they cannot conceal anything from God because their deeds are not hidden from Him.
THALABI:v3p311/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل هو كلام مستأنف، يعني ويكتمون الله حديثا

THALABI:v3p311/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311/r4.speaker: الكلبي وجماعة
THALABI:v3p311/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi and a group explain that they cannot conceal anything because the keepers of Hell testify against them.
THALABI:v3p311/r4.anchor: الكلبي وجماعة: لا يكتمون الله حديثا لأن خزنة جهنم تشهد عليهم.

THALABI:v3p311/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p311/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reconciles the denials in 6:23 with this verse: after seeing Muslims forgiven, polytheists deny shirk, then their limbs testify and they wish to be buried in the earth.
THALABI:v3p311/r5.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس، فقال: أشياء تختلف علي في القرآن

THALABI:v3p311/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p311/r6.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v3p311/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says people pass through different Judgment scenes: silence, lying, confession, asking for mercy, and finally sealed mouths with speaking limbs.
THALABI:v3p311/r6.anchor: الحسن: إنها مواطن، ففي موطن لا يتكلمون ولا يسمع الا همسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r1.claim: In yawmʾidhin, yawm is an adverb attached to idh; the tanwin compensates for an omitted genitive clause. Idh normally takes a following nominal or verbal clause, as in the cited examples.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r1.anchor: ودخل التنوين في إذ بدلا من الإضافة، وذلك أن أصل هذا أن تكون إذ مضافة إلى جملة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r2.claim: The kasra on the dhāl in idh is not case marking, even if idh is genitive; it breaks the two adjacent still consonants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r2.anchor: فكسرت الذال لالتقاء الساكنين فقيل: يومئذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r3.claim: A poetic line ending “and you were then sound” shows idh used without anything preceding it, supporting the claim that its kasra is phonetic rather than case marking.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r3.anchor: نهيتك عن طلابك أم عمرو ... بعاقبة وأنت إذ صحيح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r4.speaker: القطامي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r4.claim: Al-Qutami's line illustrates idh attached to a clause beginning with a nominal predicate, as in the grammatical construction under discussion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r4.anchor: وقال القطامي (¬4): إذا الفوارس من قيس بشكتها ... حولي شهود وما قومي بشهاد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p521#2/r5.claim: The author refers to his earlier discussion of yawaddu at 2:96.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r1.claim: They wish to become dust and merge with the earth into one thing.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r1.anchor: أي يكونون ترابا، فيستوون معها حتى يصيروا وهي شيئا واحدا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r2.claim: They will not conceal anything from God when, after denying their deeds, their limbs testify against them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p127#2/r2.anchor: هذا حين سئلوا فأنكروا فشهدت عليهم الجوارح

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r1.claim: At that time means on that Day; the people wished this after disobeying the Messenger in worldly life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r1.anchor: أي: في ذلك اليوم { يود الذين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r2.claim: They wish they could become dust and merge with the earth as one substance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r2.anchor: أي: يكونون ترابا، فيستوون مع الأرض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r3.claim: They cannot conceal anything from God because their deeds are visible to Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:42/r3.anchor: لأن ما عملوه ظاهر عند الله لا يقدرون على كتمانه

ELMALILI:4:41-42/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r3.claim: Those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish they had been covered level with the earth, leaving no trace.
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r3.anchor: keşke yere geçmişler, üzerleri düzlenmiş, kendilerinden hiçbir eser kalmamış olsa idi diye arzu edecekler

ELMALILI:4:41-42/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:41-42/r4.claim: They cannot conceal anything from God because their mouths will be sealed and their hands and feet will speak, as Sura Yasin relates.

MAJAZ:v1p126/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p126/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p126/r7.claim: The image is that they would enter the earth until it rose over and covered them.
MAJAZ:v1p126/r7.anchor: لو تسوى بهم الأرض» (41) : لو يدخلون فيها حتى تعلوهم.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:42/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:42/r1.claim: Those who chose disbelief and disobeyed the Prophet will wish the earth swallowed them, unable to conceal anything from God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:42/r1.anchor: Küfür yoluna sapıp peygamberi dinlemeyenler o gün, Allah’tan hiçbir haberi gizleyemez hale düşerek yerin altında kaybolmayı temenni ederler.

NAHHAS:v1p456/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p456/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p456/r8.claim: Yawmaʾidhin is an adverb, optionally treated as indeclinable; idh is indeclinable and its tanwīn compensates for an omission.
NAHHAS:v1p456/r8.anchor: ظرف وإن شئت كان مبنيا و إذ مبنية لا غير والتنوين فيها عوض مما حذف

NAHHAS:v1p456/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p456/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p456/r9.claim: The wāw in ʿaṣaw is vowelled with ḍamma to avoid two sukūns, though kasra is also allowed.
NAHHAS:v1p456/r9.anchor: ضمت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين ويجوز كسرها

NAHHAS:v1p456/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p456/r10.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v1p456/r10.claim: One explanation is that the disbelievers wish they had never been raised: had they not been raised, the earth would have remained level over them, since they were made from dust.
NAHHAS:v1p456/r10.anchor: قال أبو جعفر قد ذكرناه وقيل معناه لو لم يبعثوا لأنه لو لم يبعثوا لكانت الأرض مستوية عليهم

NAHHAS:v1p456/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p456/r11.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v1p456/r11.claim: Qatāda says the Resurrection has several stages; once matters are clear and they are reckoned, they will not conceal anything.
NAHHAS:v1p456/r11.anchor: وذكرنا قول قتادة أن القيامة مواطن ومعناه أنهم لما تبين لهم وحوسبوا لم يكتموا

ITQAN:v3p72/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports a questioner bringing Ibn Abbas apparent conflicts about polytheists’ denial, questioning in the afterlife, the creation sequence, and the wording “was Allah.”
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق في تفسيره أنبأنا معمر عن رجل عن المنهال بن عمرو عن سعيد بن جبير قال جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس

ITQAN:v3p72/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p72/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p72/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that polytheists deny their shirk hoping for forgiveness, but God seals their mouths and their limbs disclose what they did.
ITQAN:v3p72/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس أما قوله ﴿ ثم لم تكن فتنتهم

ITQAN:v3p73/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas’s answers show that these passages differ by circumstance or meaning rather than contradicting one another; each was revealed as intended.
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.anchor: فما اختلف عليك من القرآن فهو يشبه ما ذكرت لك وإن الله لم ينزل شيئا إلا وقد أصاب الذي أراد

ITQAN:v3p73/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.speaker: الحاكم
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.claim: Al-Hakim transmitted the full Ibn Abbas report and authenticated it; Ibn Hajar says its original is also in an authenticated collection and groups its questions into four apparent discrepancies.
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.anchor: أخرجه بطوله الحاكم في المستدرك وصححه

DAMGHANI:v1p30/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r5.claim: Al-arḍ can mean the grave, as in the disbelievers’ wish to be levelled with the earth.
DAMGHANI:v1p30/r5.anchor: الثامن : الأرض يريد به القبر قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

ITQAN:v3p74/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p74/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p74/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq that the polytheists first deny shirk, then God seals their mouths and their limbs testify; al-Dahhak transmits the exchange through Ibn Jarir.
ITQAN:v3p74/r2.anchor: فيما أخرجه ابن جرير عن الضحاك بن مزاحم أن نافع بن الأزرق أتى ابن عباس فقال
